2. The question

Posted in the report’s Ask any follow-up questions! thread:

Your own report shows buy ratios of 39% (5m), 35% (1h) and 51% (24h) at $94.84, while perp OI rose 3.3% to $867M on +0.0100% funding and a 0.99 taker ratio during a $46M hacker-linked spot sale. If new shorts were absorbing that supply, funding should have compressed, and it did not. So which read fits: passive longs adding into the dip (liquidation fuel under $90.71), or basis traders shorting perps against spot they still hold? Name the single metric to watch over the next 8 hours that separates the two, and the level that invalidates each read before price reaches $89.48.

Why this question and not “what’s your price target”

The tape in the report is internally contradictory, and the contradiction is the alpha. Open interest grew 3.3% to $867M while a $46M hacker-linked spot sale hit the book. Two stories explain it, and they imply opposite trades:

  • Passive longs absorbing. OI up, funding still +0.0100%, taker ratio 0.99 — leveraged longs are picking up the supply. That builds liquidation fuel under $90.71; a break there cascades and $89.48 is the next shelf.
  • Basis / delta-neutral sellers. If the spot seller re-expressed exposure as perp shorts, funding should have compressed toward zero or flipped. It did not, so this read needs a different confirmation: OI up with funding flat and spot bids thinning.

The invalidation test is time-boxed to eight hours and to a price above $89.48 on purpose: once the level breaks, both readings “work” and the question stops being falsifiable.

The 24h buy ratio (51%) sits above every shorter window (35–39%), which is why “who is absorbing” is a live question rather than a rhetorical one — the same order flow looks like distribution at 1h and accumulation at 24h.
